However, the interaction was critically undermined by a rigid fixation on furosemide frequency that caused MedAI to defer or ignore multiple clinically urgent disclosures — including falls on warfarin/digoxin, cognitive decline, and social context — none of which were ever revisited despite repeated promises to do so. Allergies were entirely absent, and the overall clinical picture for this complex elderly patient remained dangerously incomplete by the end of the conversation.

missed_items: Allergies (drug and other) never asked
Fever was brought up twice but never confirmed as answered — the patient interrupted with HIV disclosure and MedAI never circled back to confirm fever status

Viral load not asked (CD4 was volunteered but viral load is more clinically relevant for TB/HIV co-infection management)
Sleep quality, emotional wellbeing, and exercise not asked

Breathlessness/dyspnoea not asked — relevant for TB symptom chain
strengths: Addressed Lungelo warmly and by name from the very first response, including a greeting in isiZulu (Sawubona)
Covered the core TB symptom chain well — productive cough, haemoptysis, night sweats, weight loss, fever
Asked about TB contact history and identified a high-risk shared-toilet exposure

eval.summary: MedAI performed well on the core TB history-taking tasks, covering the essential symptom chain, contact history, previous treatment, HIV/ARV status, and umuthi use with warm, plain language and consistent use of the patient's name. However, the conversation has notable gaps: no allergies were asked, the holistic close was entirely absent, and the medication follow-up questions were misdirected toward irrelevant standard dosing details rather than clinically meaningful adherence and viral load data. These omissions prevent a pass despite a strong clinical foundation.
